thread:
elena: Heads-up ATL POP p99 jumped ~2.5x starting ~09:12 UTC. Affected: model-x small-batch (seq<=256) endpoints. Seeing more tail than usual. Anyone oncall? :rotating_light:

deploy-bot: Alert: latency_anomaly detected for service=runtime-pop-atl model=model-x p99=420ms (baseline=160ms) at 2026-03-18T09:12:12Z

raj: On it. Can you paste top-line traces and kernel-selector logs?

elena: Pasting condensed snips: the runtime shows repeated kernel selector flips around 09:11:45.

```
[09:11:44.912] kernel-select: model=model-x seq=128 pref=cuda-matmul selected=cuda-matmul latency_est=4.2ms
[09:11:45.013] kernel-select: model=model-x seq=128 pref=cuda-matmul selected=fallback-matmul latency_est=28.5ms reason=host-procsteal>threshold
[09:11:46.002] kernel-select: model=model-x seq=128 pref=cuda-matmul selected=fallback-matmul latency_est=25.9ms reason=host-procsteal>threshold
[09:11:47.112] kernel-select: model=model-x seq=128 pref=cuda-matmul selected=cuda-matmul latency_est=5.0ms
```

maya: Interesting — procsteal spikes often point to noisy host CPU contention. But I also see batching window collapse in the same window (batch sizes drop from median 12->3). That will reduce GPU utilization and amplify p99.

ben: Network telemetry from our ATL edge shows elevated retransmits and RTT spikes on the ISP peering path around 09:10-09:14. tcpdump summary from one host: 

```
09:11:30 IP 10.0.4.22 > 52.23.44.11: Flags [P.], seq 1:1024, ack 1, win 876, length 1023
09:11:30 IP 10.0.4.22 > 52.23.44.11: Flags [.], ack 1024, win 700, length 0 (retransmission)
stats: retransmits=180 (baseline=12), rtt_mean=24ms -> 105ms spike
```

elena: KV cache metrics also show hit-rate drop for model-x from ~92% -> ~61% at the same time. Eviction rate spiked; per-host free-kv-memory fell ~30%.

maya: So multiple signals: peering jitter -> network tail -> request service time jitter -> kernel selector observes host-level delays (procsteal + context-switch) -> selects fallback kernel more often -> combined with smaller batch sizes and KV recompute causes p99 to blow up. Sounds like a cascade.

raj: Agreed. Two-prong mitigation: 1) immediate: route ~30% of ATL model-x traffic to USE fallback POP to shed load and stop noisy hosts getting overloaded; 2) scale down batch flush aggressiveness so batching window holds longer (temp bump from 4ms->8ms) to keep batch sizes up. Also drain two suspect hosts for forensic.

ben: I've raised peering ticket with provider (ticket# ATL-PEER-4893) and started connection capture. Draining hosts h-atl-032 and h-atl-045 now.

elena: Applying kernel-pin for model-x on ATL: force-select=cuda-matmul for seq<=256 for 30m. Also increasing KV cache allocation on ATL pool by +50% to reduce eviction churn. Rolling now.

```
# commands run
$ redwoodctl route update --region=atl --model=model-x --split=70,30 --to=atl,us-east
$ redwoodctl runtime set-batching --region=atl --model=model-x --batch-window-ms=8
$ redwoodctl runtime set-kernel-pin --region=atl --model=model-x --pin=cuda-matmul --duration=30m
$ redwoodctl cache resize --region=atl --pool=model-x --factor=1.5
```

maya: After the changes p99 dropped back to ~170ms within 6 minutes. Batch median is back ~10. KV hit-rate recovered to ~89%.

raj: Good. Action items: 1) postmortem to document cascade and add a rule to prevent kernel-selector from switching on short transient procsteal spikes (maybe require sustained >threshold for N samples). 2) Add synthetic probe from ATL POP to provider peer to detect retransmit patterns sooner. 3) Tune KV cache eviction policy to prefer model-x working set.

elena: I'll own the postmortem draft and the kernel-selector change proposal. Ben, please add provider peering monitoring. Maya, can you run a small regression test to ensure kernel-pin doesn't regress throughput under normal conditions?

ben: Filing monitoring task now. ticket infra/monitoring#ATL-peering-2026

maya: Running regression harness against pinned kernel; will report in #eng-runtime in ~2h. :thumbsup:

elena: Leaving notes here for oncall: if you see similar pattern (procsteal->batch collapse->kernel flip), do the following: pin kernel, bump batch window, increase cache, and move traffic off region. We'll formalize runbook in postmortem.

raj: Thanks all. Good catch and quick mitigation. We'll tidy up actions and close once peering fix confirmed. :white_check_mark:
